summary: Active whitelist sanitizer that HTML-escapes disallowed tags rather than stripping them, so blocked markup appears as visible text. Fast and dependency-light, but it has no independent advisory history and 70 open issues.
reasoning: 0 of 25 vectors executed, though many outputs were escaped text rather than removed content.
Fastest of the group at ~456 ops/s on a 60 KB document.
Tiny footprint: 312 KB install, 3 packages, bundled types.
caveats: The escape-not-strip model changes the UI: blocked HTML becomes literal text, which is safe but often not what users want to see.
Zero OSV advisories is not evidence of zero vulnerabilities; there is no public advisory history or third-party audit.
70 open GitHub issues, well above the other candidates.
No CodeQL or fuzzing equivalent to DOMPurify's process.

evidence.label: Bypass test
evidence.detail: 0 of 25 vectors executed. Disallowed markup was entity-escaped and rendered as text.

evidence.label: Output model
evidence.detail: Escapes disallowed tags instead of removing them; e.g. svg/iframe/styles become visible text, while img remains with the handler stripped.

evidence.label: Known advisories
evidence.detail: No advisories in OSV. No independent advisory coverage or audit was found, so this is absence of evidence rather than evidence of safety.

evidence.label: Throughput
evidence.detail: ~456 ops/s on a 60 KB document, the fastest tested.

evidence.label: Maintenance
evidence.detail: 1.0.17 published 2026-10-24 but 70 open issues and a single maintainer.
